---
title: "Week 13: Idiomatic Rust"
---

## Introduction

This week covers three tools you will see in almost every Rust program. Closures are small functions that capture values around them, and iterators chain steps like `filter`, `map`, and `sum` over a collection. Smart pointers (`Box`, `Rc`, and `RefCell`) handle the cases ordinary ownership cannot, and `Result` with the `?` operator makes errors part of a function's signature. One idea ties the week together: Week 10's three levels of access, read, change, or own.

## Recommended readings

- [Chapter 13: Functional language features](https://doc.rust-lang.org/book/ch13-00-functional-features.html) - Closures and iterators, session 1
- [Chapter 15: Smart pointers](https://doc.rust-lang.org/book/ch15-00-smart-pointers.html) - Box, Rc, and RefCell, session 2
- [Chapter 9: Error handling](https://doc.rust-lang.org/book/ch09-00-error-handling.html) - Result and the ? operator, session 2
